papers.title: ATHENA: Knowledge-guided agentic neural architecture search for AutoFormer-based electronic health record modeling
papers.summary: ATHENA uses collaborating AI agents and knowledge from previous hospital studies to design Transformer models for electronic health records. Reusing pretrained model components makes the search more efficient, while adapting each architecture to the clinical task and target hospital.
papers.author_preview: Deyi Li*, Qi Xu* et al.
papers.equal_note: * Deyi Li and Qi Xu contributed equally.
papers.subtitle: Knowledge-guided agentic neural architecture search for AutoFormer-based electronic health record modeling
papers.image_alt: ATHENA framework showing how source-hospital architecture knowledge guides three collaborating search agents at a target hospital.

papers.title: SMART: a new patient similarity estimation framework for enhanced predictive modeling in acute kidney injury
papers.date_note: Published online 8 August 2025; assigned to the January 2026 issue. Use 2026 as the formal citation year.
papers.summary: SMART identifies clinically similar patients by accounting for missing measurements and optimizing how different clinical features contribute to similarity. Evaluated at two hospitals, the framework improved personalized acute kidney injury prediction compared with three baseline methods in internal and external validation.
papers.author_preview: Deyi Li, Alan S. L. Yu et al.
papers.subtitle: A new patient similarity estimation framework for enhanced predictive modeling in acute kidney injury
papers.image_alt: SMART framework combining overlap weighting, distance optimization, and feature-type weighting to retrieve similar patients for acute kidney injury prediction.

papers.title: Clustering analysis of multi-site electronic health records reveals distinct subphenotypes in stage-1 acute kidney injury
papers.summary: Seven-day kidney function trajectories from 53,565 patients across eight hospitals revealed three distinct forms of stage-1 acute kidney injury. These groups had different mortality and kidney disease outcomes, showing that even clinically mild injury can conceal meaningful differences in patient risk.
papers.author_preview: Deyi Li, Ho Yin Chan et al.
papers.subtitle: Clustering analysis of multi-site electronic health records reveals distinct subphenotypes in stage-1 acute kidney injury
papers.image_alt: Original trajectory plot showing median serum creatinine before and after AKI onset for three subphenotypes, with shaded first-to-99th percentile ranges.

papers.title: LLM-as-a-Judge in Healthcare: A Scoping Analysis of Applications, Methods, and Human Alignment
papers.display_title: Can AI judges evaluate healthcare AI?
papers.summary: A review of 134 studies maps how large language models evaluate healthcare AI, from clinical documentation to medical reasoning. It examines evaluation methods and agreement with human experts, identifying where automated judging shows promise and where validation remains essential.
papers.author_preview: Lingyao Li*, Deyi Li* et al.
papers.equal_note: * Lingyao Li and Deyi Li contributed equally.

papers.title: DT-BEHRT: Disease Trajectory-aware Transformer for Interpretable Patient Representation Learning
papers.summary: DT-BEHRT organizes electronic health records around disease trajectories, capturing interactions within organ systems and changes across visits. Its graph-enhanced Transformer learns patient representations for clinical prediction, with attention patterns designed to support interpretation through disease-centered reasoning.
papers.author_preview: Deyi Li, Zijun Yao et al.

papers.title: DeepJ: Graph Convolutional Transformers with Differentiable Pooling for Patient Trajectory Modeling
papers.summary: DeepJ connects medical events across visits to model a patient's evolving health history. Its graph learning and pooling modules identify related clinical event clusters and improved mortality and acute kidney injury prediction in two retrospective datasets.
papers.author_preview: Deyi Li, Zijun Yao et al.

papers.title: Autoencoder-Based Representation Learning for Similar Patients Retrieval From Electronic Health Records: Comparative Study
papers.display_title: What makes a useful patient representation?
papers.summary: A comparison of five autoencoder designs across two hospital datasets examines how learned patient representations support similar-patient retrieval. Results highlight the importance of distance measures and learning rates, while showing that representation learning does not consistently outperform using the original clinical features.
papers.author_preview: Deyi Li, Aditi Shukla et al.

papers.title: Analyzing and Mitigating Model Drift in Acute Kidney Injury Prediction for Hospitalized Patients
papers.summary: Clinical prediction models can lose accuracy as patient populations and practice patterns change. This study tracks acute kidney injury prediction across a decade and compares population-wide and subgroup-specific updates to help maintain reliable performance over time.
papers.author_preview: Zijian Xu, Deyi Li et al.

papers.title: A Comparative Analysis of Patient Similarity Measures for Outcome Prediction
papers.summary: What makes two patients clinically similar? Using records from 46,968 hospitalized patients, this study compares four weighting strategies for outcome prediction. Optimizing weights across feature types produced the strongest similarity measure overall, informing how to build cohorts for personalized models.
papers.author_preview: Deyi Li, Alan S. L. Yu et al.

papers.title: Population Pharmacokinetics Modeling of Vancomycin Among Chinese Infants With Normal and Augmented Renal Function
papers.summary: Infants with different kidney function may clear the same antibiotic differently. This study develops and validates population pharmacokinetic models of vancomycin, examining how body weight and kidney function markers contribute to individualized concentration predictions.
papers.author_preview: De-Yi Li, Ling Li et al.
